title: Supercharge your real-time data ingestion: What's new in Fabric Eventstream connectors
summary: Microsoft rounds up a set of recent Eventstream connector updates spanning private-network connectivity, Apache Kafka and Azure Service Bus source connectors, certificate-based authentication, IoT Hub metadata handling, Oracle CDC, and HTTP pagination, with each feature's GA-versus-preview status called out.
audience: Data engineers and security/network architects deciding whether Fabric Eventstream can now reach private/on-prem sources securely, or evaluating specific connectors (Kafka, Service Bus, Oracle CDC, IoT Hub, HTTP) for production real-time ingestion.
why_it_matters: Several of these features (private network support, Kafka/Service Bus connectors, custom CA/mTLS) move from preview to general availability in this post, which is the signal enterprise/regulated customers need before relying on them in production; others (IoT Hub metadata, Oracle CDC, HTTP pagination) remain preview and should be scoped accordingly.
takeaways: Private network (vNet/on-premises) support for Eventstream connectors is now GA, built on a 'Streaming virtual network data gateway' concept.
The Apache Kafka and Azure Service Bus source connectors are now GA, with the Kafka connector gaining SASL_SSL support.
Custom CA and mTLS support is now GA across MQTT, Apache Kafka, AWS MSK, and Confluent Cloud source connectors.
Three features remain in preview: enhanced IoT Hub metadata preservation, an Oracle Database CDC connector, and HTTP connector pagination support.
The enhanced IoT Hub connector is built on the Kafka Connect framework and exposes system metadata via a distinct field-name prefix.

claims.text: Private network (vNet/on-premises) support for Eventstream streaming connectors has moved from preview to general availability, letting connectors reach sources in private Azure virtual networks or on-premises environments without public internet exposure.

The private network capability is built on a Streaming virtual network data gateway, a Fabric construct that provisions a bridge Azure virtual network/subnet so Eventstream connectors run inside the customer's network; connectivity to the private source itself is established via VPN, ExpressRoute, private endpoints, or network peering as appropriate.
The Apache Kafka and Azure Service Bus source connectors for Eventstream have both reached general availability.

The GA Apache Kafka connector adds support for the SASL_SSL security protocol alongside its existing SSL support, combining SASL-based authentication (e.g. PLAIN or SCRAM) with TLS encryption for connecting to production Kafka clusters.

Custom CA and mutual TLS (mTLS) support, previously preview, is now generally available for the MQTT, Apache Kafka, AWS MSK, and Confluent Cloud source connectors, letting customers supply their own CA and client certificates from Azure Key Vault for mutually authenticated encrypted connections.

An enhanced Azure IoT Hub source connector, in preview and built on the Kafka Connect framework, preserves full device-to-cloud message metadata (such as device ID, enqueued time, and auth method) by copying it into user metadata, prefixing system metadata keys with '__src__' so it can be distinguished from user-defined properties.

The enhanced IoT Hub connector's preserved metadata can be extracted in an Eventstream SQL operator using a GETMETADATAPROPERTYVALUE function, enabling scenarios like per-device latency monitoring and conditional routing based on device identity.

A new Oracle Database Change Data Capture (CDC) source connector for Eventstream, in preview, streams database changes from on-premises or cloud-hosted Oracle databases and can route processed change events to Eventhouse, Lakehouse, Activator, or custom endpoints.

The Eventstream HTTP source connector now supports pagination in preview, natively walking through multi-page REST API responses using either page-based (page number/size/offset) or cursor-based (continuation token) pagination configurations.
